newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Korea Yukong extends reformer shutdown to end-June.
newsitem.headline: Korea Yukong extends reformer shutdown to end-June.

text.p: South Korean oil refiner Yukong Ltd has extended the shutdown of its 8,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) reformer No. 1 until the end of June due to weak gasoline demand, industry sources said on Monday.
"It is still shut down...and now is scheduled until the end of June," a source said.
The secondary refining unit which processes naphtha into reformate for either gasoline blending or further production into petrochemical BTX, was originally closed on January 24 due to poor margins.
"It (the shutdown extension) is not so much bad margins but weak demand for gasoline," a source said.
A source last month said domestic demand, around 150,000-bpd, was 50,000-bpd lower than earlier projections.
"Gasoline demand grew by two percent in February (year-on-year) which is very low," agreed Young-Seok Moon, director of petroleum policy division of the Korea Energy Economics Institute.
"But it is a bit early to evaluate the weakness of domestic demand," he said.
Moon said demand was dampened early this year when pump prices were increased following its deregulation on January 1.
But last week prices at South Korean pumps started dipping in what some analysts described as the start of a price war.
"We expect a price decrease next month with weaker international oil prices," Moon said.
But Yukong, the country's largest refiner at 810,000-bpd, has become increasingly more active into exporting gasoline barrels into neighbouring Japan and Taiwan.

A company statement last week said Yukong, the first South Korean refiner to export gasoline to Japan since liberalising its oil imports in 1996, planned to raise its annual exports to Japan this year by 100,000 barrels to 700,000 barrels.

Yukong currently sells 400,000 barrels annually to Zen-noh, Japan's Nationwide Federation of Agricultural Cooperative, and is targetting the remaining 300,000 barrels to Japan's distribution, trade and refining companies.
Yukong also became an aggressive seller to Taiwan and just late last week was awarded Taiwan's tender for 95-octane unleaded reformate for first-half May delivery.
It sold its first cargo to Taiwan for March 16-30 delivery.
